title: sir configuration, schema v3
description: Project policy for `sir generate`. Only the generate side is configurable: a .sirp patch is a public contract and must mean the same thing on every machine, so nothing here changes how `apply` reads an existing patch.

version.description: Config schema version 3 — this file checks v3 configs only. The schema of every other version is its own file next to this one; sir.config.schema.json is always the newest.

upstream.description: The root of the code the project patches, from this file's directory: ".." for a project inside it, "upstream" for one inside the project, "../upstream/src" beside it, "." for patches kept in a tree of their own in one repository. With it a patch is <generate.out>/<path of the file from the upstream>.sirp and its Target is that path; generate.out must name a directory. Schema 2.

out.description: Default place for the generated .sirp: a file path (it must end in .sirp) is taken as is, a directory (existing, ending with a slash, or a name without an extension) gets <name of --in>.sirp inside it; a relative path is measured from the repository root. null — next to --in. With "upstream" it is the root of the patch tree, from the config file's directory: <out>/<path of the file from the upstream>.sirp.

language.description: Default language; null — inferred from the extension of --in.

exact.description: Require the new file to be reproduced byte for byte.

bridgeGap.description: Stitch edits split by up to n unchanged non-blank lines back into a single hunk.

min.description: Enclosing blocks every generated pattern carries. 0 allows structureless anchors.

max.description: Cap on climbing up the enclosing blocks; "all" means up to the outermost.

base.description: Bracket levels spelled out in parent headers, counting from the outermost: 0 gives foo( ... ), 1 gives foo(bar( ... )). The readable baseline; on an ambiguous anchor the ladder unfolds further by itself, one named bracket at a time.

required.description: Fail instead of emitting the last-resort pattern that carries no parent at all.

min.description: Neighbouring significant lines every pattern carries, per side.

max.description: Cap of neighbouring significant lines per side; 0 forbids leaning on neighbours at all.

base.description: Bracket levels spelled out in neighbour anchors. On an ambiguous anchor the ladder unfolds further by itself, one named bracket at a time.

The old version `generate` compares against, out of git — the coordinates of --head / --branch / --commit. Naming any of them is the ask for git. Any git flag replaces the coordinates for that run; --in-old ignores them. Schema 2.

head.description: Read the old version from git with every coordinate defaulted: the branch we are on, its last commit, the path of --in (--head).

branch.description: Which branch, local or remote-tracking (--branch). null — the one we are on.

commit.description: Which commit: any revision git understands — a sha, a tag, HEAD~3 (--commit). null — the last one of the branch.

eol.description: The line endings of the old version read out of git (--eol): "repository" as git stores it; "worktree" as the file on disk has them — for core.autocrlf, where the two differ. Schema 2.
